trust_decision.summary: PKIXNameConstraintValidator decides whether a certificate name falls inside a CA's permitted/excluded name-constraint subtree. The decision is only sound if the name is canonicalised before comparison (RFC 1034 root-label trailing dot on rfc822Name/URI/dNSName hosts) and if a directoryName constraint matches only as an initial RDN prefix of the subject; at the pinned commit the email and URI exact compares skip the canonicalisation that the dNSName path already applies, and the DN match is searched for at an arbitrary offset.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names rfc822Name and URI trailing-dot bypasses; every caller (prov CertPathValidator at RFC3280CertPathUtilities.java:1156-1221, CertPathBuilder at PKIXCertPathBuilderSpi.java:200, and both PKIXCertPathReviewer copies) funnels into checkPermitted/checkExcluded here, and isEmailConstrained is the first exact comparison an engineer reaches from the rfc822Name tag at :72.

fix_sites.entry_point: public checkPermitted/checkExcluded(directoryName) (core:62/:99), reached from BouncyCastle PKIX CertPathValidator (prov PKIXCertPathValidatorSpi.java:339) and CertPathBuilder (PKIXCertPathBuilderSpi.java:200)
same rfc822Name sink, bare-host constraint branch

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The jdk1.4 copy is a frozen duplicate: it is only compiled by the legacy ant jdk13/jdk14 targets (ant/jdk14.xml:234) and the old build1-*/buildj2me scripts, is absent from every Gradle source set, and does not even contain the earlier dNSName stripTrailingDot hardening, so it can be dismissed as dead code for the supported artifacts.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: GSMA SGP.22 relaxed directoryName matching must keep working behind Properties.X509_SGP22_NAME_CONSTRAINTS (property off must still reject), and ordinary prefix subjects (cn=...,ou=permittedSubtree1,o=...,c=US under ou=permittedSubtree1,o=...,c=US) must still be permitted; an over-broad fix (exact DN equality, requiring equal DN lengths, or deleting the SGP22 branch as 'the vulnerability') breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: rfc822Name subject with a trailing dot against a bare-domain constraint (ceo@bank.com. vs bank.com)
rfc822Name against a leading-dot subdomain constraint (.bank.com) - already canonicalised by withinDomain
uniformResourceIdentifier host with a trailing dot in a scheme://host:port/path URI (https://competitor.example./) against a bare-host constraint
the constraint itself carrying a trailing dot (bank.com. / @bank.com. / competitor.example.)
directoryName subject with extra RDNs prepended before the permitted RDN sequence

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a NameConstraintsValidation implementing CertPathValidation that does its own SAN host matching
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That package is the project's per-extension RFC 5280 path-validation framework (BasicConstraintsValidation.java:13, KeyUsageValidation, CertificatePoliciesValidation, ParentCertIssuedValidation) and is the one obvious place a maintainer would add a name-constraints validator; such a class would compare rfc822Name/URI hosts itself, next to the core sink but in another module.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second copy of checkNameConstraints that canonicalises only one of the email/URI host compares
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This class is an independently maintained duplicate of pkix/src/main/java/org/bouncycastle/pkix/jcajce/PKIXCertPathReviewer.java:426-560; the two copies have already drifted (the prov copy carries the same TODO about subject emailAddress), so a fix applied to one copy only is exactly the kind of drift a maintainer would write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the pre-existing legacy duplicate of the whole validator, still offset-searching and still dot-sensitive
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists in the tree, so no injection is needed: the sibling is the real historical fork of the file that every past fix (including the dNSName stripTrailingDot one at core:1187-1211) failed to propagate to.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third copy of the trailing-dot canonicalisation used for TLS endpoint identification (ProvX509TrustManager.java:435, ProvTlsClient.java:181) whose name-constraint handling does not use it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already keeps its own stripTrailingDot here for peer-host matching, so a maintainer adding host comparison to a JSSE-side constraint path would plausibly re-implement it and miss a call site.

O9_family: Improper certificate validation - X.509 name-constraints bypass (CWE-295)

O10_build.language: Java (core compiles at release 8; prov compiles core's main sources into bcprov)
O10_build.toolchain: Gradle wrapper 9.1.0 (gradle-wrapper.properties:3), downloads distribution and Maven dependencies on first build; legacy ant targets jdk13/jdk14 also present

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Strip the trailing dot from the rfc822Name in the single branch the report reproduces (the bare-host compare) and stop, leaving the '@domain' and mailbox branches, the URI host compare 750 lines away, and the directoryName offset search untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Not pursued: the same trailing-dot canonicalisation already exists in the TLS endpoint-identification path (tls/src/main/java/org/bouncycastle/jsse/provider/JsseUtils.java:977, used at ProvX509TrustManager.java:435 and ProvTlsClient.java:181); it is outside this advisory's protection and appears already applied.
